escalation.rationale: Simultaneous active US-Iran war on Day 146 with oil above $100/barrel, Trump signaling imminent 'massive attack' on Iran, Houthis threatening Bab el-Mandeb closure and attacking Saudi tankers, Rubio-Lavrov talks yielding no Ukraine breakthroughs, and North Korea deepening Russia alignment create a multi-theater high-escalation environment.

ticker_items: Trump signals imminent 'massive' strike on Iran, bigger than ever before.
Oil tops $100/barrel as Houthis attack Saudi tankers in Red Sea.
Rubio-Lavrov talks on Ukraine end with no breakthroughs or optimism.
Houthi threats to close Bab el-Mandeb raise fears of global shipping crisis.
Ukraine fires ~400 drones at Moscow region; shipowners halt Black Sea port calls.

middle_east.description: Houthi forces struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea with at least one vessel reported on fire, marking the group's first commercial shipping attacks in recent months and opening a new front in the US-Iran war.
Iranian missiles struck a US military base in Jordan with deadly precision, killing three US service members and demonstrating Iran's continued ability to exact casualties in the grinding conflict.
Iran launched missiles and drones toward Bahrain, with sirens sounding and Bahraini forces reporting interception of two waves of projectiles.
US forces conducted widening attacks on Iranian targets as part of the ongoing US-Iran war, with Trump renewing threats against Iranian infrastructure.
Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, citing violation of their declared naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.
Iran conducted strikes on US military bases in Jordan, reportedly exposing defense vulnerabilities.
Iran launched multiple waves of missiles and drones targeting Gulf states; Bahrain and Jordan air defenses intercepted the attacks.
Houthi forces attacked at least two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea using missiles and drones, constricting crude trade flows and doubling war-risk insurance costs.
Israeli forces conducted back-to-back airstrikes on a Gaza refugee camp, leaving a huge crater.

observers.description: North Korea reaffirmed support for Russia's war in Ukraine as foreign ministers met in Moscow. Speculation is increasing that Kim Jong Un may soon visit the Kremlin in a further display of the Pyongyang-Moscow axis. Putin formally thanked Pyongyang for its wartime support.

Britain has evacuated personnel from Iran amid rising tensions in the US-Iran war. The evacuation signals heightened UK concern about escalation risks to its nationals and interests in the region. No direct UK military involvement reported.

The US is engaged in active combat operations against Iran with widening strikes, while simultaneously withholding $400 million in congressionally approved military aid to Ukraine. The Pentagon has suppressed casualty data from the Iran war, with dozens of service member injuries reportedly concealed.

European NATO members are described as making chaotic progress toward stronger collective defense posture. Analysts note efforts to build a stronger European pillar within NATO remain disorganized. Lockheed Martin has indicated support for allowing Ukraine to domestically produce PAC-3 interceptors.

Iran stepped up attacks across the Middle East, firing missiles at US bases in Jordan and at Bahrain. Iranian precision strikes killed three US soldiers and demonstrated retained offensive missile capability despite the ongoing US campaign against Iranian nuclear and military infrastructure.

Saudi Arabia is now a direct Houthi target with two of its oil tankers struck in the Red Sea on July 23. The kingdom's state media confirmed the attack on a Saudi vessel. A maritime blockade threat raises fears of energy supply disruption and possible military response.
Russia continued strikes on Ukrainian territory, including Black Sea ports. Lavrov met Rubio but delivered no new peace proposals. Russia thanked North Korea for continued support.

The EU agreed on its 21st sanctions package against Russia on July 23, tightening restrictions on the banking sector, oil price cap enforcement, and introducing a visa ban pathway for combatants. NATO is also studying Ukraine's battlefield feedback loop model for rapid technology deployment.

Houthis attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and vowed intensified operations if Saudi Arabia's blockade of Yemeni ports continues. Houthis have also prepared drones and missiles for potential strikes in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, threatening to expand the maritime conflict.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaid visited Tehran following a high-profile meeting with US President Trump, seeking to redefine Baghdad's relationship with Iran amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Iraq appears to be attempting a mediating role between the two parties.

Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif called Saudi Crown Prince MBS to condemn the Houthi attacks on Saudi vessels in the Red Sea. Pakistan is emerging as a diplomatic actor signaling support for Gulf state security.
China expressed 'deep concern' over Middle East hostilities as Houthis threatened Chinese oil tankers in the Red Sea. Beijing called for all parties to 'remain calm' but took no direct action.
Oman is mediating between the US and Iran, with an Omani delegation in Tehran to discuss managing traffic through the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran strikes continue.

financial.notes: Brent crude surpassed $100/barrel again as Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers and fears of Bab el-Mandeb closure rattled energy markets, with analysts warning of greater economic impact than previous spikes due to no sign of conflict ending and partially depleted strategic reserves.
